steps.content: Days later, you and Enfer finally step inside the Belphegor Art Museum again.
Sunlight pours in through the glass and shines evenly over the chaos in the museum. Dust and debris float in the air like lost moths struggling to find light.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Well, this place is surely in ruins.
Even without the bewildering magic, you still recognize you're in the exhibition hall where Sosia was displayed.
But all the art exhibits in the exhibition hall have been wrecked into pieces, not just Sosia.
You vaguely recall Enfer has said that the works displayed in this hall are like a record of her own growth.
Actually, we can leave this to the end...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It's okay. I'm not that vulnerable.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: "The heart can melt even sadness."

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: You've seen it before.
Yes, neither of us needs to cry.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: That's right.
Enfer puts down the tools in her hands and picks up a fragment, examining it carefully.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Sleeper Under Fear. Apparently, it reminded many viewers of sleepless nights troubled by nightmares.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But I guess now it can finally have a good night's sleep.
Sweeping away the debris of different materials, Enfer gathers the fragments of this piece in a corner, piling them up.
This is like a home for all the slumbering art.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: "Under the heavy weight, you and I are both within the iron frame. The bars seem so brittle and delicate, yet impossible to break..."

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But when the night passes, the iron frame finally snaps...
Watching Enfer piecing her art together among the fragments, you suddenly feel sorry for her. You pass her a tissue and apologize to her.
I'm sorry. Perhaps I was too self-absorbed with my proposal.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Why would you think that?
I know you treat your art like your children... Asking you to face this kind of... this kind of situation directly, maybe it's kind of cruel.
I didn't think it through.
Enfer takes the tissue and shakes her head slightly.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: You don't have to apologize. I asked to come with you.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Also... you don't need to feel sad for me.
Enfer comes to the platform that was used to display Sosia, lifting her head and staring as if Sosia is still standing there.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: How empty...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Even her friends who once kept her company have all become broken pieces.
Enfer gently picks up a white fragment which used to be part of a small sculpture surrounding Sosia, probably an eye.

options: Do you want to repair her?
You will create even better works.

choices.text: Do you want to repair her?
You will create even better works.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Repair?
These are all your favorite works, aren't they?
Of course, I believe you will certainly create something even more perfect than this in the future...
But I know you love her very much.
Enfer smiles and says nothing. You think she's still hesitating, so you continue.
We've already resolved the Witching Hour. She won't be an issue.
The Sinners have already brought all sorts of bizarre belongings to the Bureau anyway. It's only one more sculpture, I think... Nightingale won't say no.
But I know these are all your favorite works.
We've already resolved the Witching Hour. They won't be an issue.
The Sinners have already brought all sorts of bizarre belongings to the Bureau anyway. It's only one more sculpture, I think... Nightingale won't say no.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: So you want me to repair them?
You love them very much, don't you?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Indeed.
Enfer nods at you and picks up a bunch of fragments.
But you find that she's not repairing Sosia, but carving something new with her hammer and chisel instead.
You hear lots of clinks and clanks, but they don't bother you at all. You lean against the platform and listen to the sound peacefully.
It sounds like a beak knocking on an eggshell.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: ...Huff.
A moment later, the sound stops. You lift your head and see Enfer propping up her face on the platform and staring down at you with a smile.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I thought you fell asleep.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Come and see my work, will you?
She reaches out a hand to you, pulling you up like inviting you to dance.
Next to her are a few small sculptures carved with the fragments.
What... are these?
The broken pieces have been sculpted and polished by Enfer and turned into several cocoon-like objects.
But the irregular shapes make you feel like something is struggling inside them.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Just some artistic residue.
They're one of a kind.
But even you can tell that these small sculptures... are indeed nothing close to Enfer's previous works.
You don't know how else to console Enfer, so you pick up the small sculptures and examine them carefully.
You see that in the center of each sculpture, there's a tiny heart-shaped mark.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: You can be more honest with me.
Enfer raises her hand and taps on one of the sculptures lightly. The cocoon falls instantly.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: These things... can't even compare to what I made three years ago.
You're... exaggerating.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: No, I'm not.

Enfer scans the empty exhibition hall. The room filled only with broken fragments is like an airtight prison. Suffocating and heart-wrenching, it feels impossible to break free from it no matter how hard you try.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But that's nothing to be afraid of.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: That's... how an artist should be.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: As we create, we struggle, we grow, we go back to zero, and eventually we evolve into our complete form.
Enfer spreads her arms, flying up the blue fabric of her dress. You feel as if you're seeing a pair of wings lined with shiny scales.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: The works we created are the proof that we tear ourselves apart time after time.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Like breaking one cocoon after another, eventually, a stunningly beautiful moth is born.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: And...
She turns back and looks at you, smiling.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: After impressing everyone, it'll plunge into the flame and leave the world with a perfect residue.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: These artworks...
Enfer hands a fragment to you. It's a piece of alabaster with pure coloration. Its sections are rough, but the outer surface is finely polished.
The dented carved lines resemble a veil on a woman's body blown by the wind. A heart-shaped mark is also hidden among them.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: These are the cocoons artists shed off, or the marks left by a fire that destroyed everything...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Even if they're completely broken, they're proof that the artist once existed.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It's just that... fragments tend to be forgotten by the world.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: That's why... I want to create an unforgettable, perfect mark.
The fragment is being crushed in Enfer's hand, falling through her fingers.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: No matter what perplexity lies ahead... I'll destroy it.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Haha... You're so adorable.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Thank you, I guess.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: After all, I've made the decision to crush the perplexity troubling me.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Sosia has failed, and I'm stuck in a bottle right now.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But that doesn't mean I'll keep failing. Just like how I crushed Sosia, I'll find the reason for my weakness, crush this bottle, and break the cocoon once again.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: No matter how much pain I'll have to endure.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: That being said...
Enfer drags out the word, making you a little nervous.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: If we don't start cleaning up soon, I'm afraid we'll experience the Witching Hour again.
You shrug and begin tidying the place with Enfer again.
As you're working, you pay extra attention and notice that there's also a heart-shaped mark on the fragments of other works as you expected.
You recall what Enfer said and suddenly realize that if an artwork is a mark left in this world by the artist...
Then likewise, the marks on these works are also the traces the artist wanted to leave in the world!
So what exactly... do they mean?
Hmm... but this painting...?
You pull out several fragments from under the rubble and piece together an oil painting.
You've seen this painting in the Witching Hour. From the strokes, you can tell this was painted when Enfer was very young.
But it's not its immaturity that makes it special... This painting doesn't have that heart-shaped logo on it.
Holding the painting, you come next to Enfer.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Oh? You found it.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: How nostalgic...
If I guess it right... You painted this when you were little?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Yes, when I was very young... When my mother was still alive.
Mother...
Enfer, did you realize that... there's a special mark on all of your works?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Mark...?
Right... A heart-shaped mark.
And not just the works displayed here...
You pick up the cocoon-shaped sculpture on the platform and show Enfer the mark.
You even unconsciously carved this mark on the pieces you casually made just now.
Enfer takes the painting and sculpture, examines them carefully for a while, then speaks again.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: This painting... was painted when I was very young. It's a copy of a photo...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: You know, my mother was an oil painting artist, and I learned some oil painting techniques when I was little.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But... ever since my mother passed away, I've almost never painted again.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: To organize the Witching Hour, I dug out all of my works, and this exhibition hall happened to be missing an oil painting.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I found this painting by chance and filled the empty spot with it.
But there isn't that heart-shaped mark on this painting.
Enfer touches the mark on the sculpture, frowning slightly.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: But...

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Why did I carve this mark on it...?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: It seems to have crept into my bones, branding this mark in the depths of my consciousness.
Enfer bows her head, as if wanting to burn a hole in the painting with her gaze.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I left this mark on my works unconsciously. But why?

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: And when did I...
Enfer places the painting on the platform and stares at it for a moment before turning to you.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: I want to know what this mark really means.
You left this mark unconsciously. Sosia also said there was something you had been unwilling to let go of...
I'm wondering... could this be the source of your perplexity?
Enfer's eyes light up and she looks at you with a surprised and thrilled look on her face.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Then... are you willing to go and search for this source with me?
Before hearing your answer, Enfer grabs your hand.

steps.speaker: Enfer
steps.content: Come, go home with me!
